correctness.rationale: The stipulated disjoint-pair graph is the usual inclusion-model H(5,2) by complementing the labels on the second shore. In this cubic graph the threshold is 2 neighbors in S for each vertex outside S, so complementation is a cardinality-reversing bijection between minimal global offensive alliances and maximal dissociation sets. For a dissociation set of size d, the cut contains 3d-2e(D)>=2d and at most 3(20-d) edges; equality at d=12 requires a matching on D and an independent complement. Both copies of the pairs avoiding one label give the five specified matchings. The exhaustively reproduced all-set coefficient vector is [1,20,190,1080,3985,9784,15910,16600,10390,3460,564,60,5], and facet counts are (8:65,9:540,10:234,12:5). Heredity validates the single-addition maximality test. Complementing sizes gives exactly 5 z^8 + 234 z^10 + 540 z^11 + 65 z^12. Distinct extremizers intersect on only six vertices; deleting one point from each of their 12 vertices produces sixty distinct eleven-sets, exhausting the eleven-sets. The 240 action maps partition the 844 facets into 12 orbits as listed. The comparison to the strong alliance variant should be read as strict majority in the closed neighborhood (3 rather than 2 here), not strict majority among the three open neighbors; the numerical definition is unambiguous.
correctness.verification: The bounded replay enumerated all 2^20 subsets, also tested minimal alliances directly, checked all 60 unique extensions and reproduced the orbit sizes. Separate automorphism backtracking found order 240, agreeing with the natural subgroup; the frozen claim only needs that subgroup. Run the replay path with python3. No uploaded code was executed. The computation does not generalize the census to other graphs.
